panels.title: Node Ready
panels.description: Kubernetes node Ready condition from kube-state-metrics.

panels.title: CPU utilization
panels.description: Actual CPU busy %. Compare with load & IO pressure to tell 'busy' from 'stalled'.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: Used = 1 - MemAvailable/MemTotal (accounts for reclaimable cache).

panels.title: Data fs (/var) used
panels.description: Fullness of /var — Talos's writable data partition (holds container/pod data). Talos has no writable '/'.

panels.title: Uptime (since last boot)
panels.description: Time since last reboot. A recent, unexpected drop here = a node rebooted (e.g. a Talos upgrade).

panels.title: Load average (1m)
panels.description: Counts running AND uninterruptible (D-state) tasks. High load + low CPU% + high IO-pressure = an I/O stall, not compute.

panels.title: CPU — utilization and where the time goes
CPU utilization by node
panels.description: Total CPU busy %.

panels.title: CPU iowait % by node
panels.description: Time cores idled waiting on disk/NFS I/O. The block-I/O half of a stall (pairs with IO pressure below).

panels.title: CPU softirq % by node
panels.description: Kernel soft-interrupt time — network/crypto (e.g. WireGuard) lives here. Invisible to per-pod CPU; only shows at the node level.

panels.title: Memory used % by node
panels.description: Used % (MemAvailable-based).

panels.title: Memory available by node
panels.description: Absolute headroom before reclaim/OOM pressure.

panels.title: Filesystem used % (writable mounts)
panels.description: Fullness of writable data filesystems (e.g. /var on Talos). Read-only system partitions are excluded.

panels.title: Disk throughput by node (physical disks)
panels.description: Read (up) / write (down) on physical disks. Note: NFS traffic is NOT here — it's on the network panels.

panels.title: Disk busy % (utilization)
panels.description: % of wall time each physical disk was busy. 100% = the device itself is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Network — node uplink (every torrent/NFS byte crosses here)
Uplink throughput by node (RX up / TX down)
panels.description: Physical NIC throughput in bits/s. On a 1GbE node, sustained ~1Gbps here is the hardware ceiling — and NFS + WireGuard both traverse it.

panels.title: Pressure (PSI) — % of time tasks were stalled waiting on a resource
Node IO pressure — FULL (all tasks stalled on I/O)
panels.description: FULL = % of time EVERY runnable task was blocked on I/O — pure wasted time. The saturation signal.

panels.title: Node IO pressure — SOME (any task stalled)
panels.description: SOME = % of time at least one task was blocked on I/O. Early warning.

panels.title: Node CPU pressure — SOME (tasks waiting for CPU)
panels.description: CPU has no FULL by definition. High SOME = CPU oversubscribed.

panels.title: Node Memory pressure — FULL (reclaim stall)
panels.description: FULL memory pressure = thrashing. Non-zero usually precedes an OOM.

panels.title: Top workloads by pressure (per-pod cgroups, cadvisor)
Top pods — IO FULL pressure (now)
panels.description: Which pod's cgroup is stalling on I/O. A pod value ABOVE its node's FULL value = the stall is that pod's, not shared.

panels.title: Top pods — IO FULL pressure over time
panels.description: History of the worst I/O-stalled pods.

panels.title: Top pods — CPU pressure (now)
panels.description: Pods waiting on CPU.

panels.title: Top pods — CPU pressure over time
panels.description: History of the most CPU-starved pods.

panels.title: Top pods — Memory FULL pressure (now)
panels.description: Pods stalling on memory reclaim — best early warning for an OOM-kill.

panels.title: Top pods — Memory FULL pressure over time
panels.description: History of memory-stalled pods.
